title: What does the XRPL NoFreeze account flag mean?
abstract: Sourced explanation of NoFreeze and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, NoFreeze permanently gives up individual trust-line freezing and the ability to clear GlobalFreeze. [1]

The option cannot be disabled after activation. It does not mean every existing global freeze is automatically cleared or that a token has no remaining issuer-related risks. Read its interaction with GlobalFreeze and clawback before activation. An irreversible account setting needs an explicit issuer decision because later operators cannot simply toggle it back. [1][2]

XRPL distinguishes an AccountSet option from the AccountRoot bit that records the resulting state. SetFlag and ClearFlag use option identifiers, while the ledger Flags field stores bit values; the numbers are not interchangeable. Read the documented mapping for NoFreeze and check the validated account state after any permitted change. A successful submission response alone does not establish that the requested state is final. [1][2]

Author interpretation: document why NoFreeze is needed, who may authorize a change and what existing users would experience. Review irreversible settings before issuance and test reversible settings with representative counterparties. This is guidance for interpreting account controls, not a live network measurement. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
